newsitem.title: RUSSIA: FOCUS-Unknown Monblan wins third of Russia's YUKOS.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Unknown Monblan wins third of Russia's YUKOS.

text.p: The Russian government sold its stake in a major domestic oil company on Monday when an unknown investment firm acquired 33.3 percent of YUKOS for $160.1 million.

"YUKOS has become the first private oil company. The state has just 0.1 percent of the shares, which have not been sold at auctions," Konstantin Kagalovsky, deputy chairman of the bank heading a commission selling the shares told a news conference.

The 745.66 million shares were bought by ZAO Monblan, unknown in Russian corporate circles, for just $100,000 more than the starting price in a process reminiscent of the opaque and controversial shares-for-loans auctions in 1995.

ZAO Laguna, backed by Menatep Bank won the right to control the stake in a shares-for-loans auction last December, though the stake remained in government ownership. The deal gave Laguna the right to sell the stake from September 1 1996.

Laguna's winning bid to manage the holding was $159 million, so Monday's auction produced a tiny book profit for the sale of a stake in one of Russia's biggest oil companies, a firm with massive reserves.
Kagalovsky said Monblan was unrelated to Menatep Bank, which organised the latest auction of the shares.
"There is no connection between Monblan and Menatep. They are different organisations," he told reporters, adding he had no information about when or by whom Monblan was established.

A second, lower bid was lodged by Moscow Food Combine, affiliated with the Rosprom group, which unites Menatep's industrial holdings. Foreign investors may own not more than 15 percent of a Russian oil company so they could not bid.
Monblan must invest $200 million in YUKOS, one of a dozen vertically integrated Russian oil companies, over two years.

The auction is the latest link in a convoluted chain of privatisation of Russia's biggest companies, many of them in the potentially lucrative energy sector. It was the first time shares acquired under the shares-for-loans scheme had been sold.
The winners of the original auctions were free to sell the shares from September 1.
Menatep said last month that Rosprom held a 52 percent controlling stake of Yukos, through Laguna.
The shares-for-loans scheme was highly controversial and several auctions were won by companies close to the organisers and at prices little more than the starting price.
Critics accused the cash-strapped government of selling strategically important stakes at absurdly low prices.
Russia later pledged to end large-scale privatisation in favour of a case-by-case approach. However, controversy still dogs the sell-offs.

The State Duma lower house of parliament last week urged a halt to a cash auction, due to close on Monday, for 8.5 percent of national power company Unified Energy System, saying the cash generated would not compensate for the loss of control over a strategically important industry.
The State Property Committee and Federal Property Fund said the auction would go ahead, with results known by January 17.
YUKOS, whose main operating units are Yuganskneftegaz and Samaraneftegaz, said last week its 1997 oil output would fall 6.8 percent to 32.6 million tonnes.
Yuganskenfetgaz output would fall to 24.6 million tonnes from 26.37 million and Samaraneftegaz outout would slip to eight million from 8.62 million tonnes.
